The finding is real. I checked it in a scratch shared clone at 7b5dbd7, then deleted the clone.

(1) The mutant survives. I applied sed to certify.py:619, changing `"encoder_budget": max([16384, *map(int, batched)])}` to `"encoder_budget": 16384}`, and ran `apps/infrx-api/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration/backend/test_certify.py`. The tail was `29 passed in 1.01s`. The only encoder-budget cases change the dict or the record's flags (test_certify.py:452 and :481). The serve.sh drift block (:487-499) edits only the image and ENGINE_MAX_NUM_SEQS, and asserts only {runtime_image, engine_max_num_seqs}. Nothing in the tests reads the budget from serve.sh.

(2) The pin fails open. I copied models/marlin2b into scratch, added a flag after `--max-num-seqs "$ENGINE_MAX_NUM_SEQS"`, and called config_problems(current_config()). Output: `base 16384` / `literal 32768 True` / `var 16384 False`. With `--max-num-batched-tokens "$BATCHED"`, the regex `--max-num-batched-tokens[ =]+\"?(\d+)` finds no digits, so the reader falls back to 16384 and the pin passes. That quoted-variable form is how serve.sh already writes `--max-num-seqs "$ENGINE_MAX_NUM_SEQS"`, so it is the likely way decision B would be written.

Why it is not blocking:
- At 7b5dbd7 and on claude/backend-impl, serve.sh and serving-version.json have no --max-num-batched-tokens flag.
- 0117d48 (decision B at 82 s) adds only evidence and result rows. No launch-script change has landed yet.
- The main pins do not depend on serve.sh: the record's digest is recomputed and the published release is checked against the record.
- A deployed engine running a different batched value would still fail `inventory_problems`, which requires exactly the served flags ("flags the engine runs beyond the pin").

So what is exposed is only the tree-level second source. It is a coverage gap and a latent fail-open against the F6 docstring, not a wrong result today. It should still be fixed before the decision-B serve.sh change lands. The proposed fix is right:
- add a batched-tokens drift in the test and assert 'encoder_budget_tokens' is in the names;
- make serve_sh_pins return None when the flag has no integer literal;
- register the mutant in e4b_mutants.py.

A literal `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` was read as 32768 and the problem names included 'encoder_budget_tokens'. So the certify config pin passes a raised budget when serve.sh sets it through a variable.

Why it is nonblocking: the property that matters is that serve.sh cannot drift from the record, and another test already enforces it. The shipped serve.sh has no --max-num-batched-tokens flag. apps/infrx-api/tests/w/test_serving.py::check_pinned_launch runs serve.sh itself and requires the flags after the image to equal served_flags(record) exactly (line 114). I added `BATCHED=32768` and `--max-num-batched-tokens "$BATCHED"` to serve.sh and ran `$PY -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/w/test_serving.py`. The tail was 'tests/w/test_serving.py:114: AssertionError ... FAILED tests/w/test_serving.py::test_perf_pilot__the_engine_starts_pinned_on_loopback_with_the_recorded_flags ... 1 failed, 7 passed in 5.97s'. A serve.sh that raises the budget while the record stays unchanged therefore fails make api-test whichever way the flag is written.

The certify serve.sh read was never a complete flag comparison anyway: current_config recomputes engine_options_digest from the record, not from serve.sh. What remains is a missing killing test and a lenient regex in certify's secondary check, not a way for drift to get through the checks. The proposed fix is still worth doing: add the drift case, return None when the flag value is not a literal integer, and add the mutant to e4b_mutants.py.
